LESSON: EFFECTIVE

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Story Telling By the end of the sub-strand,  Learners listen to stories and mod
Topic 1.3: Effective

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Effective
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. use compound and complex whole class talking to has SPEAKING sentences to link thoughts  Learners participate in play both in understood our
2. listen to concerns and opinions  Learners share their opinions and of others and represent them in represent the views of others to an appropriate forum relevant authorities e.g. child abuse
3. demonstrate willingness to interact with others
4. appreciate the importance of sharing one another’s feelings

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Effective

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Effective

Teach
• Focus skill: use compound and complex whole class talking to has SPEAKING sentences to link thoughts  Learners participate in play both in understood our.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Effective.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Effective
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
